About the Green Climate Fund
The Green Climate Fund (GCF) is the world's largest dedicated climate fund and supports developing countries in pursuing low-emission and climate-resilient development pathways.

The Accreditation and Entity Relations Unit (AERU) within the Department of Investment Services supports Accredited Entities (AEs) throughout the accreditation lifecycle and partnership journey with GCF. This includes onboarding newly accredited entities, institution-level reporting under the Monitoring and Accountability Framework (MAF), advisory and capacity-building services, particularly for Direct Access Entities (DAEs), communications, knowledge management, and support for institution-level compliance and partnership obligations.

The Secretariat of the Fund seeks to recruit a Consultant to support the Accredited Entities Advisory team and Country Ownership activities within the Department of Investment Services (DINVS). The consultant will join DINVS at the GCF headquarters in Songdo, Republic of Korea. The assignment is for an initial period of 240 days over 12 months with the possibility of renewal.
Position Objective

The objective of the assignment is to ensure continuity of Accredited Entity onboarding, institution-level reporting, advisory services, DAE support initiatives, country ownership and related stakeholder engagement and knowledge-management.
The consultant will provide technical expertise, coordination support, and operational leadership to maintain delivery of agreed work programme priorities.
The Consultant will report to the Head, Accreditation and Entity Relations or their delegate.
The Consultant will work closely with colleagues across accreditation, programming, portfolio management, legal, readiness, regional, and policy teams, as appropriate.
Duties and Responsibilities
1. Accredited Entity Onboarding and Partnership Support
Support onboarding of newly accredited entities and formalization of institutional partnerships.
Coordinate follow-up actions related to accreditation conditions, framework agreements, standard conditions, and other institution-level requirements.
Support Accredited Entities in understanding and meeting institution-level obligations and reporting requirements.
Facilitate coordination among relevant Secretariat teams to support Accredited Entity readiness and progression toward programming activities.
2. Institutional Reporting and Monitoring Support
Coordinate institution-level reporting processes led by AERU under the Monitoring and Accountability Framework.
Finalize draft standard operating procedures and templates for institutional reports;
Support report notification, submission tracking, completeness review, technical assessment coordination, communication of outcomes, publication follow-up, and recordkeeping.
Review Accredited Entity submissions and provide technical analysis and recommendations, specifically on Environment and Social Safeguards.
Support preparation of management briefings, internal assessment materials, and Board reporting inputs.
Contribute to improvements in reporting processes, tools, templates, procedures, and quality-control arrangements.
3. Direct Access Entity Advisory and Capacity-Building Support
Support implementation of initiatives that strengthen Direct Access Entity institutional capacity.
Contribute to development and delivery of advisory services, technical assistance activities, and capacity-building initiatives.
Coordinate with internal and external partners delivering support to Direct Access Entities.
Contribute to implementation of initiatives supporting Direct Access Entity engagement and institutional strengthening.
4. Communications, Outreach, and Knowledge Management
Support development of guidance materials, knowledge products, learning resources, and communication materials.
Contribute to accreditation monitoring and accountability, and aforementioned DAE-related outreach and stakeholder engagement activities.
Maintain institutional records and documentation associated with onboarding, reporting, advisory support, and capacity-building activities.
Develop lessons learned, operational recommendations, and knowledge products to strengthen future service delivery.
5. Operational Coordination and Transition Support
Coordinate activities among technical reviewers, consultants, and relevant Secretariat teams involved in entity reporting and support activities.
Monitor progress of key workstreams and identify operational risks and mitigation measures.
Maintain documentation of ongoing activities and stakeholder engagements.
Prepare handover materials and support knowledge transfer to the incoming staff member.
6. Country Ownership
Support implementation of the new Country Ownership Guidelines through practical tools, monitoring approaches, and Secretariat-wide operational guidance.
Support NDA-led country portfolio review mechanisms that strengthen accountability, learning, and continuous country engagement.
Support implementation and learning from country platforms to strengthen country-led investment planning and coordination.
Support creation of practical mechanisms that make country ownership visible during implementation and decision-making.
Expected Results
Continuity of Accredited Entity onboarding activities.
Final Standard Operating procedures for Institutional Reporting
Final Reporting templates and guidance published and circulated to AEs
Timely administration of institution-level reporting processes.
Continued support to Accredited Entities, with a focus on strengthening programming capacity of Direct Access Entities.
Effective coordination of cross-functional review processes.
Retention of institutional knowledge.
Support to onboarding of the incoming Accredited Entities Advisory Principal.
Scope Limitations
The Consultant will provide technical, advisory, coordination, and operational support. Unless specifically authorized in writing, the Consultant will not:
Exercise formal supervisory authority over GCF staff.
Conduct performance management activities.
Approve personnel, procurement, budget, or contractual decisions.
Exercise authorities reserved for staff members under GCF policies and procedures.
Serve as the final decision-maker on institutional reporting determinations or management approvals.
Qualifications
Advanced university degree in economics, environmental studies, finance, business administration, international development, public policy, climate change, or a related field.

At least 3 years of relevant professional experience in accreditation, Environmental and Social Safeguard, Gender, institutional assessments or reporting, climate finance, capacity development, multilateral organizations, or related areas.
Demonstrated experience managing complex review processes involving multiple stakeholders.
Strong analytical, drafting, communication, coordination, and stakeholder-engagement skills.
Experience supporting institutional reporting, monitoring frameworks, compliance processes, portfolio analysis, or capacity-building programmes is desirable.
Fluency in English required. Knowledge of another United Nations language is an asset.
Contract Period and Duty Station: Twelve (12) months, based at the GCF Headquarters in Songdo, Republic of Korea.
